name: Smart token management for long context
gist: These papers reduce the memory explosion when models process very long documents by deciding which tokens matter most and keeping only those, or using clever ways to summarize.
explain: Attention in transformers has a quadratic cost: if a document has 100 tokens, attention is 100 squared, which equals 10,000 operations. At 1 million tokens (a very long book), attention alone is a trillion operations. For long documents, memory explodes because you have to store all those attention scores. But not all tokens matter equally. Early in a document, the model might not need to see every single word — it could focus on key sentences. Later, when making a specific decision, only a few previous tokens matter (the ones already seen). Why load and process every token when you can be smart about which ones to keep?

These papers tackle smart token selection in several ways. One approach is pruning: as you process the document, mark tokens as important or not, and drop the unimportant ones from memory. Another is summarization: condense the already-processed part of the document into a shorter summary, then process new tokens with attention to just the summary plus a recent sliding window. A third is routing: only certain tokens get full attention, others get reduced attention, based on what the model predicts will matter. These techniques can shrink the effective length of the document from a million tokens to maybe 10,000 or 100,000, making processing tractable.

The hard part is deciding which tokens to keep without losing important information. If you drop a token that turns out to be critical, the model's answer gets worse. Researchers use multiple signals: frequency (common words might matter less), position (first and last tokens in a passage matter more), or learned importance scores. Some papers use auxiliary networks that predict which tokens will be important, adding a bit of overhead now to save huge overhead later. The goal is to handle multi-million-token documents in reasonable time without degrading the quality of the model's output.

papers.title: CoMem: Context Management with A Decoupled Long-Context Model
papers.contribution: Provides 1.4x latency improvements on SWE-Bench-Verified while preserving performance, with favorable scaling under increased system throughput.

papers.title: FlashVID: Efficient Video Large Language Models via Training-free Tree-based Spatiotemporal Token Merging
papers.contribution: Retaining only 10% of visual tokens preserves 99.1% of LLaVA-OneVision performance; enables 10x increase in video frame input to Qwen2.5-VL with 8.6% relative improvement within same computational budget.

papers.title: LearnPruner: Rethinking Attention-based Token Pruning in Vision Language Models
papers.contribution: LearnPruner preserves 95% of performance using only 5.5% of vision tokens with 3.2× inference acceleration.

papers.title: Task-Aware Structured Memory for Dynamic Multi-modal In-Context Learning
papers.contribution: Sustains strong multi-modal ICL performance under high compression ratios by balancing efficiency, adaptability, and semantic fidelity.

papers.title: iLLaVA: An Image is Worth Fewer Than 1/3 Input Tokens in Large Multimodal Models
papers.contribution: Deliver 2x throughput boost and 4x reduction in prefilling time, enabling larger models to surpass smaller counterparts in both accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: CLIP Tricks You: Training-free Token Pruning for Efficient Pixel Grounding in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: LiteLVLM maintains 90% of original performance with 22% speedup and 2.3× memory reduction; outperforms baselines by >5% across token budgets without training.

papers.title: DND: Boosting Large Language Models with Dynamic Nested Depth
papers.contribution: Boosts dense models (Qwen3-1.7B/Llama3.2-1B/Gemma3-1B) by 1.88-2.61% and MoE models (Qwen3-30B) by 0.87% with minimal parameter/compute increase.

papers.title: Improving Visual Token Reduction via Rectifying Distortions for Efficient Multimodal LLM Inference
papers.contribution: Consistently improves accuracy of various reduction methods while maintaining computational efficiency.

papers.title: Less Is More: Fast and Accurate Reasoning with Cross-Head Unified Sparse Attention
papers.contribution: Matches or improves accuracy while attending fewer tokens; achieves 1.6× end-to-end speedup and 1.72× sparse attention speedup with kernel optimizations.

papers.title: Less Token, More Signal: MoE Expert Pruning via Critical Token Selection
papers.contribution: On 30B Qwen3 MoE at 50% sparsity, Step achieves 50% memory reduction with minimal performance loss, 1.5× throughput improvement, and completes pruning in 10 minutes.

papers.title: MMTok: Multimodal Coverage Maximization for Efficient Inference of VLMs
papers.contribution: Achieves 1.87x speedup on LLaVA-NeXT-13B while retaining 98.7% performance; maintains 87.7% performance with only four vision tokens.

papers.title: OmniFit: Bridging Modalities via Layer-Adaptive Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Retains 98% of model performance with only 20% token usage, achieving up to 2.31x end-to-end speedup and 2.5x VRAM saving across 3 model series on 10 benchmarks.

papers.title: SPLIT-VLM: Salience-Guided Partitioning towards Local Coverage for Importance-Aware Token Dropping in Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: SPLIT preserves over 99% accuracy with 192 vision tokens and 92.8% with only 64 tokens on image understanding with LLaVA-1.5-7B.

papers.title: Statistically Calibrated Scaling for Token Merging in Transformers
papers.contribution: Closed-form optimal corrections calibrate both energy balance and distributional fidelity, demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness across compression levels on vision Transformers.

papers.title: TokenDrop: Token-Level Importance-Aware Backward Propagation Skipping for Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 42.9% memory reduction and up to 1.50× training speedup while preserving accuracy and outperforming existing backpropagation-skipping baselines.

papers.title: Untied Ulysses: Memory-Efficient Context Parallelism via Headwise Chunking
papers.contribution: UPipe reduces peak activation memory by as much as 82.5% for 70B Transformers and supports maximum context lengths of 5M tokens for training 8B models on a single 8xH100 node.
